speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and have a history of easy bruising. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have ever had prolonged bleeding after other surgeries or injuries, and do you have any family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of joint swelling in your uncle is a significant clue, suggesting a possible factor deficiency rather than a platelet issue. To clarify this, do you personally have a history of deep tissue bleeding, such as bleeding into your joints or muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I need to check your clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Activity, Factor_IX_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, this rules out Hemophilia A and B. I need to check if you have Hemophilia C or another disorder, so REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_Activity, Platelet_Count, PT, aPTT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor_XI_Activity: 25% (Low), Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3 (Normal), PT: 15 sec (Normal), aPTT: 60 sec (Prolonged)

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor XI activity, prolonged aPTT, and family history confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C
